item.title: One Month After Bhotekoshi Floods, 1,453 Dead, Survivors Leave Camps
item.description: Nepal's disaster agency counts 5,285 missing while ABC News Australia reports over 5,700, as holding centres empty and rebuilding lags.

item.content:encoded:
Illustration: AI generated with gpt-image-1. Made for Nepal Wire. Not a photograph.

<p>One month after floods tore through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli valleys, Nepal's disaster authority counts 1,453 dead and 5,285 missing. Nepal Press and Tribune India both cited those figures from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority on September 26.</p> <p>Some roads and bridges are back. Nepal Press reports crews have temporarily reconnected key stretches washed out by the water. But the outlet is blunt about what that does not mean. Full reconstruction remains far off. Relief distribution, temporary housing and rental support for displaced families are still being organized, a month after the disaster hit.</p> <p>On the ground, the picture is thinner than the reconnected roads suggest. OnlineKhabar reports that holding centres set up for displaced families are emptying out. Survivors interviewed by the outlet say they received little beyond basic relief items, food and daily supplies from government and non government sources. With nothing more coming, many have left the centres and moved in with relatives instead.</p> <h2>A home built over four decades, gone in a day</h2> <p>OnlineKhabar's reporting on one family captures the scale of individual loss behind the numbers. Ishwar Basnet flew home from Portugal, leaving his six-week-old baby behind, to search for his parents. He looked for eight days. He never found their bodies. The family home, built up over 35 to 40 years, was also swept away. Basnet told OnlineKhabar he now has no house and no village to return to, only memories.</p> <p>The missing count carries its own dispute. NDRRMA's 5,285 figure, reported by Nepal Press and Tribune India, is not the only number in circulation. ABC News Australia reported on September 26 that over 5,700 people remain missing. Nepal Wire could not independently verify which figure is more current. The gap itself says something. A month after a disaster this large, Nepal still does not have one agreed number for how many people it lost.</p> <p>The hydropower sector adds another layer. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha told Parliament on September 23 that more than 800 workers from hydropower projects remain unaccounted for, according to the Kathmandu Post. That figure predates the one month mark by three days. Nepal Wire found no public update to it since.</p> <p>For Nepal Press, the verdict a month on is simple. The wounds are the same. The road to recovery is still long. Nepal Wire found no published government timeline for full reconstruction. Nor did it find any NDRRMA statement on when the missing count will be final.</p>

Sources: Nepal Press, OnlineKhabar, OnlineKhabar, Tribune India, Kathmandu Post, ABC News Australia
